source.light: Parity measurement: app_qt/shell_style.h (the wave-17/21 constants the caption band, gutter and timescale band were already painted with).  The light values are what the port rendered before W29-5.1, so the gate pins them to prove the light render did not move.
source.dark_gray: Sampled from the local audit frame corpus/reference/2026-10-23-audit/mcp-computer-use-blob-1792744264666-4mp1fn.jpg (MS Project Professional 2021, Office Dark Gray theme; git-ignored, never committed).
source.black: Sampled from the local audit frame corpus/reference/2026-10-23-audit/mcp-computer-use-blob-1792744264666-ekrn72.jpg (MS Project Professional 2021, Office Black theme; git-ignored, never committed).
source.note: The audit frames are 874x491 JPEG-downscaled captures of the same project view in the same window.  The committed palette values are the dominant flat colour of each clean run (>= 100 px away from text/rules), so the gate compares rendered pixels with these numbers exactly.  The fill values in header.* are the capture samples (see capture_samples); text inks are the brightest sampled glyph cores rounded to the chrome's measured dark text colour, and the ribbon ink is a one-ink contrast choice against the measured ribbon surface (decision 3), not a sampled Project bitmap colour.  Derived fields are marked in capture_samples.
source.sampling: build/w29/g5-w29-5-1-measure.log (local): vertical/horizontal pixel runs at fixed x/y plus per-rectangle colour modes.

derived.sheet_header_text: Both dark captures show light captions; their brightest glyph cores (#E3E4DF Dark Gray, #F3F3F3 Black) support the chrome's #F2F2F2 dark text ink.  A one-pixel caption stroke cannot reach the pure ink through JPEG downscaling, so the ink is the chrome text colour, not the sample itself.
derived.row_header_text: The row numbers are one small glyph each; their peaks (#B9B9B9 / #AFAEAC) are dimmer than the captions' only because of their size in the downscaled frame, so the gutter uses the same #F2F2F2 ink (direction measured: light on both dark fills).
derived.sheet_header_text_muted: No stub caption ('Add New Column') is visible in either dark capture; the muted ink is the theme's light ink dimmed to the chrome's black muted value #B0B0B0.
derived.sheet_header_arrow: The sort chevron is below the capture's resolution; it follows the muted caption ink (light: the measured #6A6A6A).
derived.sheet_header_grip: The resize ticks are below the capture's resolution; the light theme keeps its measured #B0B0B0 and the dark themes keep the same ticks.
derived.chart_header_weekend: No weekend tint is distinguishable in either dark chart header (sampled day-cell fills within +/-2 of the band fill), so the dark weekend shade equals the band fill; light keeps the measured #F7F7F7.
derived.chart_header_text: The dark captures' label cores (#383838 Dark Gray, #3A3A3A Black) are the file's #333333 ink; Project does not lighten the timescale labels with the theme, so neither does the port.
derived.chart_header_rule / _strong: The vertical cell rules were sampled as solid one-pixel columns: Dark Gray #5F5F5F / #545454 and Black #2D2D2D / #323232; the shade further from the band fill is the strong (week/month) rule.  The horizontal tier boundary samples match the weak rule in both themes.
derived.ribbon_ink: Decision 3: the ribbon's own one-ink artwork.  Dark Gray's measured group row #BDBDBD is light, so the wave-26 ink #1F3A5F stays (contrast 6.1:1); Black's #292929 is near-black, so its glyphs use the light #E6E6E6 (contrast 11.6:1).  Project's own ribbon bitmaps in Black are still coloured, so no Project glyph colour is copied or matched.
